At Hudaibiya the Prophet rubbed out 'Allah's Messenger' from the treaty, agreed to return pagans who came to him, and came the next year for three days with sheathed weapons.
At Hudaibiya Suhail made the Prophet agree to return anyone coming from them, so Abu Jandal was returned, but believing women emigrants were not, as a verse was revealed.
The Prophet accepts Suhail's terms at al-Hudaibiya, including returning converts; companions sacrifice and shave, emigrant women are examined, and Quraish ask him to call in Abu Basir's raiders.
At Siffin Sahl bin Hunaif recalls Hudaibiya, when Umar protested the terms to the Prophet and Abu Bakr, and after Surat al-Fath the Prophet told him it was a victory.
The Prophet's four Umrahs include al-Hudaybiya, where a dried well refills and water flows from his fingers for the 1300 to 1500 men whose pledge al-Bara calls the true victory.
Setting out with 1300 to 1500 companions, the Prophet takes Ihram; Ka'b shaves his lice-ridden head for a ransom, Umar provides for a pledger's daughter, and the Tree is forgotten.
Pledgers under the Tree say they pledged for death, the pledge verse 48:1 refers to, and report the Prophet on charity, Friday prayer and donkey meat; one rules on witr.
Marching for Umrah, the Prophet consults on Quraysh barring him and accepts Suhail's term to return their men; emigrant women are tested, and the 'manifest victory' sura is revealed.
If barred from the Ka'bah, Ibn Umar will do as the Prophet did when Quraysh barred him, sacrifice and shave; he pledged under the Tree before Umar did.
Back from Siffin, Sahl bin Hunaif recalls wanting to refuse the Prophet's order on the day of Abu Jandal; lice-ridden Ka'b is told to shave and pay a ransom.
Umar, unanswered three times while travelling at night, fears revelation about himself, but the Prophet recites the new surah on a manifest victory, which Anas says means Hudaybiyyah.
Jabir says they were one thousand four hundred on the day of Hudaybiyyah.
At Siffin Sahl bin Hunaif recalls Hudaybiyyah, when Umar protested to the Prophet and Abu Bakr against returning without fighting, and Surat al-Fath was revealed.
